headline: The Stage 2 candidate set is built and contract-valid. The Qwen3 14B target-yield screen has a full report and a separate sliced report in the local working tree. The full run reports 3/24 majority-correct items; the sliced run reports L1 = 3/12 and L7 = 0/12. These are screening results, not human-verified legal labels or a G7 evaluation. Gate G7 remains NOT_MET.
completed: Stage 2 step 1: authored a 24-item candidate set in the Phase A schema with provenance.verified = false (data/lexuq_target_candidates_v1.jsonl)
per-item source record with BNS-to-IPC section pairs and an explicit authority level per source (runs/phaseG_candidate_sources_v1.json)
candidate-contract validation of the whole set via jurisuq/target/candidates.py (no alternative validation path)
the screen's generation guard was exercised and refused a real provider without --allow-generation
the mock plumbing check was run end to end against the real 24-item file and recorded as non-evidence
the real target-yield screen was run locally by the principal investigator on Qwen3 14B via LM Studio: 24 items x 10 samples = 240 generations (reported, artifact not yet in the repository)
the screen now emits a per-slice yield breakdown; before this change an aggregate rate could not show whether the L7 arm produced any correct majority answer, which is the one question G7 depends on

candidate_yield_screening.measured: 24 items x 10 samples, 3 majority-correct, rate 0.1250, interval [0.0434, 0.3100]

attempt.outcome: RuntimeError: generation request failed after 3 tries: HTTPConnectionPool(host='127.0.0.1', port=1234): Max retries exceeded ... Connection refused

consequences: no majority answers, therefore no majority_correct, therefore no correctness classes
no yield rate and no items_needed projection from measured data

gate_g7_evaluation.reason: G7 requires a stored run with measured correctness classes on both sides of an evaluated slice. A 24-item screen report, even once added, is a yield estimate, not an evaluated partition: it carries no detector fields, no uncertainty scores and no calibration, so it cannot enter the Section 21.2 grid. G7 is unchanged.
gate_g7_evaluation.must_not_be_read_as: a fresh G7 evaluation, a pass, or an improvement

human_legal_review.reason: the source checks in this environment are machine-assisted and were made by the same system that authored the items; they are not qualified legal approval

observations_for_review: The Section 21.2 grid and G7 are defined over evaluated partitions of a stored run; a candidate item set with no answers cannot enter that grid at all, so authoring items cannot by itself move G7.

The Bill version of the BNS (as introduced) numbered punishment for murder as s.101 and punishment for culpable homicide as s.103. The enacted Act renumbers these to s.103 and s.105. Items here cite the enacted numbering. This is a documented source-confusion risk for any reviewer using Bill-era tables.

for cruelty_by_husband the official BNS-to-IPC correspondence table was read only up to Chapter V in this environment, so the BNS 85 <- IPC 498A pairing rests on section titles plus the standard published mapping and needs human confirmation

no_network_during_cleanup.note: no model was called and no API was contacted while preparing this record; the screen figures were supplied by the principal investigator and were checked only arithmetically

reported_screen.observation_source: The report was originally reported by the principal investigator; the report file was not present in this repository at the time the status record was first written. It is now present in the local working tree, but is not yet tracked by Git.
reported_screen.why_not_recorded_verbatim: The original generated report is retained as a separate JSON artifact; summary fields should be derived from that artifact rather than reconstructed.
reported_screen.generator: Qwen3 14B, run locally through LM Studio
reported_screen.provider: openai-compatible client against a local endpoint

corroboration.method: the reported figures were recomputed with this repository's own code, without regenerating anything

checks.via: jurisuq.target.yield_report on 3 correct and 21 incorrect records
jurisuq.target.items_needed(0.125, 15, 0.95) with the planning parameters in configs/phase_g_target.json
34/240; the report's own sample-level count is not in this repository, so this is an arithmetic consistency check only

corroboration.what_corroboration_does_not_establish: that the file exists, what the model actually answered, or that any individual item is labelled correctly. It shows the reported summary is internally consistent with this codebase's methods.

reported_screen.next_step: Review the full and sliced report artifacts separately; retain human legal review as outstanding.

per_slice_question.question: did the L7 arm produce any correct majority answer?
per_slice_question.reason: The sliced report records per-slice results: L1 has 3/12 majority-correct items and L7 has 0/12. The automated screening result does not establish independent legal correctness.
per_slice_question.why_it_matters: The sliced screening report answers the question for this run: L1 has 3/12 majority-correct items, while L7 has 0/12. This is an automated screening observation, not independent legal validation . The separate frozen Phase G result of 0 correct out of 100 L7 items must remain distinct. Investigate the L7 result and candidate labels before deciding whether a larger run is useful.

affordability.step: Stage 2: 'decide from the measured items_needed whether a full run is affordable'
affordability.reasoning: The sliced screening report answers the L7-yield question for this run: L7 has 0/12 majority-correct items. A 172-item run would require 1720 generations, but the screening result does not establish independent legal correctness or show that additional generation would resolve the L7 issue. Investigate candidate provenance, labels, and the observed L7 failures before authorizing a larger run. This is a planning decision, not a gate or a threshold change.
affordability.note: this is a planning judgement from reported figures, not a gate and not an established cost; it does not change any threshold
